- 2026-09-15T16:25:53.038Z — chose **1.5 input forms: `sofar event append --payload` and `sofar remember [text]` each accept the JSON/text three ways — inline as today, `-` for stdin (the quoted-heredoc form the AGENTS block now shows: `--payload - <<'EOF' … EOF`), and `@<path>` for a file; with the value omitted and stdin piped, stdin is read. `remember --supersedes <M-handle>` records `supersedes` on memory_promoted as the QUALIFIED handle `<slug> M<n>` (a bare `M<n>` resolves against the target initiative; either form is validated to name an existing memory before the append). Fold marks the superseded memory (`superseded_by`) within its own record; memory.md renders it struck with the successor named; doctor's repo-memory axis stops nagging for a superseded memory across every record and nags for its successor instead. sofar_remember gains the same `supersedes` arg.** over (a) a separate `--payload-file`/`--text-file` flag only — one more flag to learn, and the `-`/`@file` idiom already exists on `sofar import`; (b) tolerant JSON parsing (JSON5, smart-quote repair) — hides the mangling instead of removing it and makes the log's validation weaker; (c) storing `supersedes` unqualified — repo.md and doctor cite qualified handles only (repo-memory-capture D2), an unqualified one would be ambiguous repo-wide; (d) deleting or rewriting the superseded memory — history is append-only. because Round 1's CLI agents lost turns to shell quoting: apostrophes and inner quotes inside `--payload '<json>'` and `remember "<fact>"` broke the command and produced correction events. stdin under a quoted heredoc is the one shell form that carries any byte unchanged, and the payload reference already pins every example to validate, so the fix is the transport, not the parser. Supersession lets an outdated fact be replaced without a correction event that leaves doctor nagging for both.
